testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How long should it take for air pressure to build up in a single air system?
questions.explanation: In a single air system, air pressure should build from about 50 to 90 psi in 3 minutes.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: Drains water and compressor oil from the air tanks
Stops air from leaking out if the air compressor breaks
Activates the emergency brakes when there is a leak
Keeps the spring brakes in place until they are needed

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from leaking out if the air compressor breaks
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be placed between the air compressor and the first main tank. It stops air from escaping the system if the air compressor develops a leak.

questions.question: Is a low air pressure warning signal required on vehicles with air brakes?
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, brake drums should have no cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check your brake drums during the walk-around inspection. It is unsafe to drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half the width of the friction area.

questions.question: What are the two markings on a front brake limiting valve?
questions.explanation: Some older air brake vehicles made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings.

questions.question: What condition should brake linings be in?
questions.explanation: Brake linings must not be loose or soaked with oil or grease. They also should not be dangerously thin.

questions.question: What is the best way to use your brakes on a steep downgrade?

options.text: Keep the brakes pressed the entire way down
Apply the brakes for a few seconds, then release them for a few seconds. Repeat this pattern as you go down the hill
Use the brakes only near the bottom of the hill
Press the brake pedal with steady, constant pressure all the way down

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes for a few seconds, then release them for a few seconds. Repeat this pattern as you go down the hill
questions.explanation: On a long or steep downgrade, use your brakes to help the engine slow the vehicle. Apply brakes until you feel the vehicle slow down, then release them once you are about 5 mph below your safe speed. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: What can be found in the air entering air storage tanks?
questions.explanation: Air entering storage tanks usually contains water and compressor oil. These materials can damage the braking system if they build up, so tanks have drains to remove them.

questions.question: How should air tank drains be used?

options.text: The driver should not use them
Use them only when it is wet outside
Open them daily to drain the tanks completely

questions.correctAnswerText: Open them daily to drain the tanks completely
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if left in the system. You must open the manual air tank drains every day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate allowed for a double combination vehicle during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: Know the maximum safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A double combination vehicle should not lose more than 4 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: For a vehicle with air brakes, check the air compressor drive belt before each drive. What condition should the belt be in?
questions.explanation: The belt should be tight and in good condition.

questions.question: If the air pressure warning light comes on, what should you do?

options.text: Drive with one foot on the accelerator and one foot on the brake.
Safely pull off the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely pull off the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning light comes on, you must stop the vehicle safely while you can still control the brakes.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within how many seconds?
questions.explanation: Air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems within about 45 seconds.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of air in the braking system.
The pressure of air from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. Not all air brake systems have this gauge.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, what is true?

options.text: Braking will only work if there is enough air in the tanks.
You can brake 14 times before the air runs out.
Continue driving normally and check the brakes later.
Keep driving but turn on emergency flashers to warn others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking will only work if there is enough air in the tanks.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. You can only brake as long as there is enough air left in the tanks.

questions.question: A modulating control valve controls which of the following?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets the driver gradually apply spring brakes. In equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.
Be careful because the brakes may fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not apply the brake pedal if spring brakes are on. Using both air pressure and spring force together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When going downhill, brake until you reach a speed that is:
questions.explanation: Hold the brake pedal until you reach 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release it. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: A ____ allows a driver to gradually apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets the driver gradually apply spring brakes. In equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: The ____ are turned on by an electric switch triggered by the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure moves an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: Using the brakes creates heat. If too much heat is produced, what happens?

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.

questions.explanation: Brakes can handle a lot of heat, but excessive heat causes them to fade. When brakes fade, they lose their ability to slow the vehicle. You should also use engine braking to help slow down and avoid overheating the brakes.

questions.question: Emergency brakes are required on which vehicles?

options.text: Only required when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have both emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how are the air tanks arranged?

options.text: Air tanks are shared by both systems.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must designate which system you are using.
Brakes on only one side of the vehicle will work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems connected to one set of brake controls. Each system has its own air tanks.

questions.question: When do spring brakes come on?

options.text: When too much air pressure is lost.
When a control on the dashboard is activated.
When the tires have minimal tread depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: When too much air pressure is lost.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes activate automatically when air pressure drops to a dangerously low level. Do not wait for this to happen. Exit the road safely as soon as you see the low pressure warning and stop your vehicle while you can still control the brakes.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should check that the ____ come on automatically when air pressure falls below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Before driving, verify that spring brakes come on automatically when air tank pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. To test this, chock the wheels and release air by pressing the brake pedal on and off. The parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should engage.
